subject: Accessing logProb_Y for each mcmc samples

messages.author: 937253792853878c
messages.subject: Accessing logProb_Y for each mcmc samples
parts:
Dear nimble users,

I would like to extract the log-probabilities of my observation nodes Y in my model after estimating my parameters with nimble. Ideally, I would like to have the log-probabilities for each of my observations and for every mcmc samples.
I apologies in advance if I missed that part in the manual, but I didn't find how to access them a posteriori.

Thanks for your help,

Jean-Baptiste

Here is an example of how I run nimble for my model.

M1_CPG_nimble <- nimbleModel(code= M1_CPG_nimbleCode, name= 'M1_CPG_nimble',
                               constants = constants_list, data =nimble_data,
                               inits = init_ll)
## Compile model
CM1_CPG_nimble <- compileNimble(M1_CPG_nimble)

##MCMC specification
M1_CPG_nimbleSpec <- configureMCMC(M1_CPG_nimble)
M1_CPG_nimbleSpec$addMonitors(monitored_param)

## Compile for MCMC
M1_CPG_nimbleMCMC <- buildMCMC(M1_CPG_nimble)
C_M1_CPG_nimbleMCMC <- compileNimble(M1_CPG_nimbleMCMC, project=M1_CPG_nimble)

##RUn the model
n_iter <- 10
#set.seed(0)
M1_CPG_nimbleMCMC$run(n_iter)

Samples <- as.matrix(M1_CPG_nimbleMCMC$mvSamples)

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Accessing logProb_Y for each mcmc samples
parts:
Not a problem.  The log-probabilities for all model nodes are also stored in the model.  For node 'X', the current log-probability is stored in the variable named "logProb_X".

So if your monitored_param variable contains c('a', 'b', 'c'), then all you have to do is also add monitors for 'logProb_a', 'logProb_b', and 'logProb_c'.  Then build the MCMC, compile the MCMC, run it, and extract samples all the same, and you'll also have all the logProb variables in the resulting samples matrix.

As in your code, you could simply add:

##MCMC specification
M1_CPG_nimbleSpec <- configureMCMC(M1_CPG_nimble)

logProb_param <- paste0('logProb_', monitored_param)   #### NEW

M1_CPG_nimbleSpec$addMonitors(monitored_param)
M1_CPG_nimbleSpec$addMonitors(logProb_param)           #### NEW

.... etc

Let me know if that works for you!

Daniel

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Accessing logProb_Y for each mcmc samples
parts:
Two changes.

First -- what was causing the logProb_variables to not be recorded -- after arranging the MCMC configuration object to record the logProb variables, you were then  building the MCMC algorithm directly from the original model (which is allowable, but it uses all defaults, which does not record any logProbs), instead of building the MCMC according to your customized MCMC configuration object.

Second -- this wasn't an error, but was causing your MCMC to run very slowly -- you were running the *uncompiled* MCMC algorithm, which is a pure R function.  Instead (unless for the purposes of debugging), you should run the *compiled* MCMC algorithm, and also exact the mvSamples and mvSamples2 objects from the *compiled* version.

Both of those changes are made (and clearly indicated) in the attached file, which runs just fine.

Let us know how it goes!
Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Accessing logProb_Y for each mcmc samples
parts:
A further question regarding this example...

Daniel's posted code generates Samples2 with dimensions 100 x 53 - i.e. it generates LogProb outputs for 53 nodes. Nice!

Is an alternative possible where a 100 x 1 output is generated such that the single output is the total LogProb associated with the ensemble of stochastic nodes, i.e. the value that would be returned (in this example) from CM1_CPG_nimble$getLogProb()  ?

Or is the only possibility at pressent to calculate these values once the MCMC has finished?
